question: English physician John Langdon Down first described this condition as a distinct clinical entity in an 1866 paper in the London Hospital Record. Nearly a century later, a team at Paris's Armand-Trousseau Hospital including Jerome Lejeune, Raymond Turpin and Marthe Gautier discovered its cause: an extra copy of the smallest human chromosome, found in affected individuals' cells in 1959. That discovery gave the condition its clinical name, referring to a third copy of chromosome 21 instead of the usual two. It is now the most common chromosomal cause of intellectual disability, typically also producing characteristic facial features and an increased risk of congenital heart defects. For 10 points, name this genetic condition caused by trisomy of the twenty-first chromosome.
